newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Prayers end in bloody clashes at al-Aqsa mosque.
newsitem.headline: Prayers end in bloody clashes at al-Aqsa mosque.

text.p: Moslem worshippers rose from their weekly prayers at Jerusalem's al-Aqsa mosque on Friday to fresh confrontations with Israeli soldiers.
Within an hour, three Palestinians were dead and more than 60 wounded.
A 30-year-old Palestinian man, his shirt stained with blood from the casualties he helped evacuate, cursed the Israeli prime minister.
"Damn you (Benjamin) Netanyahu, what kind of peace is this?" shouted the man.

The tiny clinic below the seventh-century Dome of the Rock mosque, Islam's third holiest site, was smeared with blood. Medics bandaged the wounded and sent them off in private vehicles to Jerusalem's Makassed hospital.

Women screamed in horror as hundreds of Israel's paramilitary border police, wearing bullet-proof vests and helmets, stormed the mosque and charged demonstrators. Bullets flew in all directions as demonstrators fled for cover.

"God take revenge on you, you beasts," an elderly woman shouted as Israeli police used batons on a group of women sheltering below an arched gate of the Dome of the Rock. One woman fell to the ground while the others rushed inside the building.
The confrontation was the bloodiest at al-Aqsa since 1990 when Israeli security forces killed 17 worshippers during clashes with stone-throwing Palestinians.
Friday's violence was the latest round of Israeli-Palestinian fighting that erupted on Wednesday after Israel opened a tourist tunnel adjacent to the al-Aqsa mosque compound.
Palestinians say the tunnel weakened the foundations of ancient buildings surrounding the mosque and threatened the holy sites. Israel said the tunnel did not harm the site.
At least 53 Palestinians and 14 Israeli soldiers were killed in three days of gun battles across the West Bank and the Gaza Strip.
Israeli security forces, anticipating violence after Friday prayers, deployed thousands of security forces around the Old City of Jerusalem and at the gates to the mosque.
Witnessess said the fighting erupted when a few young worshippers began throwing stones at Israeli security forces. Israeli officials said hundreds of rocks were thrown.

Witnesses said the Israelis, stationed on buildings above the compound and at the gates, responded to the stones by unleashing barrages of live ammunition at the crowds. Many of the wounded were hit in the torso.
Ayman Idkaidek, 28, took a direct hit to his head. Another man killed was also hit in the head while the third victim took a bullet in the chest.
"Look. This is what Netanyahu is doing," said a 42-year-old Palestinian man at the hospital, displaying a piece of Idkaidek's shattered skull.
